notes.title: API rate-limit rollout plan
notes.content:
# API rate-limit rollout plan

A staged release for the public API. Keep the first change reversible and make the slow path visible.

> [!TIP]
> Start with a small cohort and keep the rollback switch ready.

## Release checklist

- [x] Add request counters and dashboards
- [x] Document `429` responses
- [ ] Enable the new limit for 10% of traffic
- [ ] Review error rate after 24 hours

| Stage | Audience | Exit signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Observe | Internal users | Metrics are stable |
| Pilot | 10% | No support spike |
| Rollout | Everyone | Runbook is complete |

notes.title: Remote interview prep — Node.js
notes.content:
# Remote interview prep

Practice explaining trade-offs clearly: **correctness first**, then latency, operability, and cost.

## Story to rehearse

I simplified a queue consumer by making retries explicit and adding idempotency keys. The result was easier to observe and safer to replay.

- Use a concrete before/after metric
- Explain the failure mode
- Name the smallest safe next step

notes.title: Architecture decision: local-first notes
notes.content:
# Architecture decision

Keep the app dependency-free and store the library in IndexedDB.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The storage layer owns validation, migrations, backup compatibility, and CRUD. The UI talks to its public API.

## Why

- Notes remain private by default
- `index.html` can open directly
- The boundary is easy to test and explain
- Import/export gives the user control of portability

notes.title: Backup and restore runbook
notes.content:
# Backup and restore

1. Export before changing browser profiles or origins.
2. Keep the JSON file somewhere safe; Nook does not encrypt it.
3. Import only a file you trust.
4. Remember that import replaces the current local library.

The backup status indicator is a reminder, not a substitute for a second copy.

notes.title: Senior engineer career principles
notes.content:
# Career principles

- Make the trade-off visible
- Write down the invariant before changing code
- Prefer small reversible steps
- Leave the next person a clear path to verify the result

A strong remote engineer communicates the reasoning, not only the implementation.

# Search and filter UX

> [!NOTE]

notes.title: Local storage boundaries
notes.content:
# Local storage boundaries

IndexedDB and localStorage are scoped to the current browser origin. `file://`, `localhost`, and another port do not share data automatically.

Use a JSON backup when moving the library between origins or browser profiles.

Test the complete flow with keyboard-only navigation before calling the interaction ready.
